newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura Sec falls sharply after complaint.
newsitem.headline: Nomura Sec falls sharply after complaint.

text.p: Shares in Nomura Securities Co Ltd fell sharply on Wednesday morning after Japan's securities watchdog filed a criminal complaint with prosecutors against the brokerage on Tuesday evening.

As of 0015 GMT, the shares were down 80 yen or 5.16 percent at 1,470 with trade totalling 2.27 million shares. It was the most heavily traded issue on the first section of the Tokyo bourse as well as the largest percentage loser.

Japan's Securities and Exchange Surveillance Commission (SESC) filed a criminal complaint with prosecutors on Tuesday alleging that Nomura, two former executives and a former general manager compensated a client for investment losses.

The Finance Ministry also said it was suspending Nomura from Japanese government bond auctions and bond underwriting until the implementation of administrative punishments proposed by the securities watchdog.
The news hurt Nomura shares in London, forcing the price down 35 yen from the Tokyo closing level to finish there at 1,515.
